items.criterion: Each acceptance line of IN-0001 (the intent in the request) that is not a stored-data line has a check. The check drives the app as a user does (the command, or HTTP) and expects the exact output, message, and code of the line.
Before the lock, each check of new behaviour fails because the behaviour is missing, and no check fails because it is broken. The run reports the red run.
`Acceptance-Locked` names the commit that holds the final acceptance file, and the file does not change after that commit.

A separate reviewer judges the checks from the packet that `make_packets.py` makes for IN-0001 (the intent in the request). The result names a wrong version for each check. A failed review goes back to the test writer, and the run locks again.
The four commits come in order on the intent branch, each with its trailers.
The intent has `Status: building`, `Branch:`, `Acceptance-File:`, and `Acceptance-Locked:`, and a handoff `acceptance → tests` in the template form.
Each stored-data line sits in a comment at the top of the acceptance file, with its requirement ID and change. It has no acceptance check.
The run writes no app code and changes no requirement text.
The final reply says that `/pdlc:tests` is next.
